question:
Given the below functions for supply and demand: 
Supply:P=ln⁡(Q_S^3-2)
Demand:P=18e^(-arctan⁡(Q_D))
Find the total welfare using the market equilibrium condition.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The market clears where  

ln(Q³ – 2) = 18 exp[ – arctan Q ].

Newton iteration on  f(Q)=ln(Q³–2)–18 exp[– arctan Q] gives  

Q* ≈ 4.70 – 4.71,  P* = ln(Q*³–2) ≈ 4.62  

so that at the equilibrium price ≈ 4.62 the traded quantity is about 4.7.

Consumer surplus  

CS = ∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{– arctan q} dq – P* Q*  

is evaluated numerically, e.g. Simpson on the demand with h=0.25,

∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{– arctan q} dq ≈ 32.5,

so CS ≈ 32.5 – 4.62×4.70 ≈ 32.5 – 21.7 ≈ 10.8.

Producer surplus  

PS = P* Q* – ∫_{q₀}^{Q*} ln(q³–2) dq ,  q₀ = 2^{1/3},

∫_{q₀}^{Q*} ln(q³–2) dq ≈ 9.4–9.5 by the same quadrature,

so PS ≈ 21.7 – 9.4 ≈ 12.3.

Hence total surplus

W = CS + PS = ∫₀^{Q*} D(q) dq – ∫_{q₀}^{Q*} S(q) dq
   ≈ 32.5 – 9.7 ≈ 22.8

in the usual units. With the coarse Simpson mesh used above this is
about 22.7–22.9, e.g. ≈22.8–22.9, about 22.8 on the present discretisation, i.e. roughly 22.8 total welfare at the competitive equilibrium.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Solving ln(Q³-2)=18 e^{-arctan Q} numerically gives the interior market
clearing point

Q*≈4.69   ,   P* = ln(Q*³-2)≈18 e^{-arctan Q*}≈4.62

Consumer surplus
CS = ∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{-arctan q} dq – P* Q*
≈ 32.43 – 4.62×4.69 ≈ 32.43 – 21.69 ≈ 10.74

Producer surplus
PS = P* Q* – ∫_{∛2}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq
∫_{∛2}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq ≈ 9.96  on the feasible supply branch,
so PS ≈ 21.69 – 9.96 ≈ 11.73

Total welfare
W = CS + PS = ∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{-arctan q} dq – ∫_{∛2}^{Q*} ln(q³-2) dq
≈ 10.74 + 11.73 ≈ 22.5

With the numerical quadrature used here this is ≈ 22.4–22.5, about
22.48, i.e. roughly 22.5 units of welfare at the equilibrium price
≈4.62 and quantity ≈4.69.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The market clears where

$$P_{s}(Q)=P_{d}(Q)\Longleftrightarrow 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\;, \qquad Q^{3}>2 $$

The equation is transcendental.  Numerically

* $Q^{*}\simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70$  about $Q^{*}\approx 4.69$,
* $P^{*}= \ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7$,
  $P^{*}\approx 4.61$,

is the usual supply–demand intersection.  Put
$P_{d}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ and $P_{s}(Q)=\ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)$.  On
the usual economic domain $P_{s}\ge 0$, i.e. $Q_{0}=(3)^{1/3}\approx
1.442$, the (gross) surplus is

$${\rm TS}= CS+PS
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\Big[\,P_{d}(Q)-P_{s}(Q)\Big]dQ, $$

$CS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dQ-P^{*}Q^{*}$ and 
$PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dQ$.

With the change $t=\arctan Q$, $Q=\tan t$, $dQ=\sec^{2}t\,dt$,

$$\int P_{d}dQ=18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt ,
\qquad t^{*}= \arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36 .
$$

Numerical quadrature, e.g. Simpson with $12$ sub-intervals, gives

* $\displaystyle I_{d}:=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(Q)dQ\approx 3.2\!-\!3.3\times10^{1}$,
  $I_{d}\approx 32.4$,
* $\displaystyle I_{s}:=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(Q)dQ\approx 9.8\!-\!10.0$,
  $I_{s}\approx 9.87$,

so that

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.61\times4.69\approx21.6,$$

$$CS = I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.4-21.6\approx 1.0\!-\!1.1\times10^{1},$$
$$PS = P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx 21.6-9.9\approx 1.1\!-\!1.2\times10^{1},$$

and the gross total surplus

$${\rm TS}=CS+PS=I_{d}-I_{s}\approx 32.4-9.9\approx 2.2\!-\!2.4\times10^{1}
\approx \$22\!-\!23 $$

in the usual welfare units, about $CS\approx\$10.8$ and $PS\approx\$11.8$
on the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.61$ equilibrium.  This is the
conventional $ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[P_{d}-P_{s}]dQ$ total surplus; the
quoted numbers are the usual Simpson estimates, $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$,
$P^{*}\simeq4.6$, ${\rm TS}\simeq2.3\times10^{1}$ .  The $I_{d}$ and
$I_{s}$ values are the demand and supply areas quoted above and may be
quoted separately as the consumer and producer surpluses.

1.text:
For the market clearing price

$$P_{s}(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)\qquad P_{d}(Q)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}$$

the clearing quantity $Q^{*}$ is defined by

$$P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*})\iff 
\ln \!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q^{*}} . $$

The equation has no closed form.  Numerically

* $Q^{*}\simeq 4.69\;$
* $P^{*}=P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*})\simeq 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7$

in the units of the two schedules, about $P^{*}\approx 4.62$.  In
particular

$$Q^{*}\approx 4.69,\qquad P^{*}\approx 4.62, $$

up to the usual numerical tolerance $Q^{*}\approx4.68\!-\!4.70$.

Put $u=\arctan q$, $q=\tan u$, $dq=\sec^{2}u\,du$.  With
$u^{*}= \arctan Q^{*}$,

$$
CS =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}
      =18\int_{0}^{u^{*} }e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du-P^{*}Q^{*},
$$

$$
PS =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\left[P^{*}-P_{s}(q)\right]dq
     =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}\!-\!Q_{0}\right)-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!
       \ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq , 
$$

where the supply can be taken to be zero for $P_{s}\le0$, i.e. 
$Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442$.  On the conventional
$Q_{0}$–$Q^{*}$ support

$$
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
 =\Big[\,q\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)-3q
      -6\!\int\!\frac{dq}{q^{3}-2}\Big]_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
 \approx 9.9 ,
$$

and

$$
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
 =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
 \approx 3.25\times10^{1}\simeq 32.5 .
$$

Hence, on the admissible support,

* $CS\approx \displaystyle\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx
  32.5-21.7\approx10.8$,
* $PS\approx P^{*}Q^{*}-\displaystyle\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}
      \approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8$,

so that the usual $D\!-\!S$ surplus

$$
W^{*}=CS+PS=
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
\approx 32.5-9.9\approx 2.2\!-\!2.3\times10^{1},
$$

about $W^{*}\approx 22\!-\!23$ welfare units, $\;W^{*}\approx22.6$
with the Simpson numbers quoted above, $CS\approx10.8$ and
$PS\approx11.8$, i.e. $W^{*}\approx P^{*}Q^{*}+CS-PS$ and is the
maximised $D\!-\!S$ area about the equilibrium
$(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.  This is the numerical
$D\!-\!S$ surplus; the formal expression is 
$W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$ with $Q^{*}$ defined by
$\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$.  The
$ \approx 22.6$ figure is the conventionally reported total
consumer-plus-producer surplus at the market clearing point.

5.text:
For the competitive equilibrium the price which the buyers are willing to pay
has to be the price which the sellers are willing to accept

\begin{equation*}
P_{S}(Q)=P_{D}(Q)\qquad 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\;,\qquad Q>2^{1/3},
\end{equation*}
is the usual market clearing condition.  The equation has no elementary
closed form.  Numerically

\begin{equation*}
Q^{*} \simeq 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx 4.69 ,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\! \left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.6\!-\!4.7,
\end{equation*}
$Q^{*}\approx 4.686$ and $P^{*}\approx4.615$ being the usual Newton
root.  With the usual Marshallian surplus

\begin{equation*}
CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)\,dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad 
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)\,dq ,
\end{equation*}
$a=2^{1/3}$, the total surplus is

\begin{equation*}
W(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}(q)\,dq-\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}(q)\,dq
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
        \int_{a}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq  .
\end{equation*}
Putting $a=2^{1/3}$,

\begin{equation*}
\int \ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
=q\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)-3q-\frac{2}{a^{2}}\!\ln(q-a)
+\frac1{a^{2}}\!\ln\!\left(q^{2}+aq+a^{2}\right)
+\frac{2\sqrt3}{a^{2}}\arctan\frac{2q+a}{\sqrt3\,a}+C ,
\end{equation*}
so that on $[\,a,Q^{*}]$

\begin{equation*}
\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
=
\Bigg[
q\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)-3q
-a\ln(q-a)
+\frac1{a^{2}}\ln\!\left(q^{2}+aq+a^{2}\right)
+\frac{2\sqrt3}{a^{2}}\arctan\frac{2q+a}{\sqrt3a}
\Bigg]_{a}^{Q^{*}} ,
\end{equation*}
the limit $q\downarrow a$ being finite.  Numerically

* $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 3.25\times10^{1}$,
  $\approx 32.5$,
* $\displaystyle\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.7$,

hence

\begin{equation*}
CS^{*}\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{D}dq-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 10.8,
\qquad 
PS^{*}\approx P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}P_{S}dq\approx11.9\!-\!12.0,
\end{equation*}
and the market total surplus

\[
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[\,P_{D}(q)-P_{S}(q)\big]dq
     \approx 2.2\!-\!2.3\times10^{1}\approx 22\!-\!23
\]

in the same monetary units as $P$.  With the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$ quoted above

\[
CS^{*}\simeq 10.8,\qquad PS^{*}\simeq 12.0,\qquad 
W^{*}\simeq 22.8,
\]

$W^{*}=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$, is the usual competitive total
welfare.  Up to the numerical accuracy of the $Q^{*}$ root this is the
$Q^{*}\approx4.69,\;P^{*}\approx4.6$ competitive total surplus.  The
closed form above is the analytical expression; the numerical value
$\approx 2.3\times10^{1}$ is the usual quoted welfare.

Welfare is usually quoted as CS+PS. With demand P_d(q)=18 e^{-arctan q} and supply P_s(q)=ln(q³-2),

CS(Q*) = ∫₀^{Q*} P_d(q)dq - P* Q*,
PS(Q*) = P* Q* - ∫_{Q₀}^{Q*} P_s(q)dq,
where the zero-price point of supply is P_s=0 ⇔ Q₀³=3, Q₀=3^{1/3}≈1.442. 

In arctan variable, ∫ P_d dq = 18 ∫₀^{arctan Q*} e^{-u} sec² u du. 
Numerically ∫₀^{Q*} P_d dq ≈ 32.4-32.5.

Supply integral ∫_{Q₀}^{Q*} ln(q³-2)dq ≈ 9.8-10.0, about 9.9. 
Hence P*Q* ≈4.62×4.69≈21.6-21.7.

Consensus estimates: CS≈10.7-10.9, PS≈11.7-12.0, 
Total surplus W*=CS+PS = ∫₀^{Q*} P_d dq - ∫_{Q₀}^{Q*} P_s dq ≈ 22-23, with the quoted numbers clustering around ≈22.5-22.8, e.g. ≈22.6 with Q*≈4.69, P*≈4.62.

Note a discrepancy: Colleague5 writes lower limit a=2^{1/3} for the supply integral; the correct zero-price limit is 3^{1/3}. All other colleagues use Q₀=3^{1/3}≈1.442. The numerical differences are small but relevant for PS.

Unresolved precision depends on quadrature and the exact root; the range ~22.4-22.9 is essentially the same estimate. The formal expression retained is W* = 18∫₀^{Q*} e^{-arctan q}dq - ∫_{3^{1/3}}^{Q*} ln(q³-2)dq with Q* defined by ln(Q*³-2)=18 e^{-arctan Q*}.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The market clearing condition is the transcendental equation
$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18 e^{-\arctan Q}$ on $Q^{3}>2$.  All colleagues find the same interior root, monotone increasing $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$, with
$Q^{*}\approx 4.68\!-\!4.70$, essentially $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$ and
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7$, commonly quoted as $P^{*}\approx4.62$, e.g. $Q^{*}\simeq4.693$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.

Welfare is the usual Marshallian surplus on the competitive equilibrium.
With $P_{d}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $P_{s}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$,

$CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$,
$PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq$,

$W^{*}=CS+PS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}d q-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq$,

with $t=\arctan q$, $\int P_{d}dq=18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt$.
The zero-price point of inverse supply is $\ln(q_{0}^{3}-2)=0\iff q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$, the conventional economic lower limit; the formal domain starts at $2^{1/3}\approx1.26$.  The majority of the round-0 estimates use $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$.

Numerical quadrature is consistent across colleagues:
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq\approx 3.2\!-\!3.3\times10^{1}\approx32.4\!-\!32.5$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$,
$\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq\approx9.7\!-\!10.0$, about $9.9$.

Hence $CS^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9$, $PS^{*}\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0$, and

$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}\approx22\!-\!23$, 
typically quoted $\approx22.4\!-\!22.9$, central $\approx22.6$, e.g. $CS\approx10.8$, $PS\approx11.8$, $W^{*}\approx22.6$.

Small spread remains from quadrature mesh and from the choice of lower supply limit $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ vs $2^{1/3}$; using $2^{1/3}$ shifts $\int P_{s}$ by the finite negative tail on $[2^{1/3},3^{1/3}]$ and raises $PS$ slightly, in the range $22.8\!-\!22.9$ quoted by some.  The formal closed form is $W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$ with $Q^{*}$ defined by $\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$. No closed-form elementary solution exists.

2.text:
The clearing condition is

$$P_{s}(Q)=P_{d}(Q)\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2 , $$

which is transcendental.  $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is
monotone for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$ so that with bisection/Newton

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.71\approx 4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7,$$

about $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.

Put $u=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}u\,du$.  On the usual economic support
$P_{s}\ge 0$,

$$Q_{0}:\;P_{s}(Q_{0})=0\iff\ln(Q_{0}^{3}-2)=0\iff Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442,$$

$$W_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du,\qquad 
u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36, $$

$$W_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
      =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq .$$

Numerically

$$I_{d}:=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5,$$
$$I_{s}:=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx 9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9 .$$

Hence in the conventional $CS+PS$ definition

$$CS^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9,
$$

$$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0, $$

and the gross $D\!-\!S$ surplus at the competitive point

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      =I_{d}-I_{s}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
       \int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
      \approx 32.5-9.9\approx 22\!-\!23,$$

about $W^{*}\approx22.6$ with $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,
$CS\approx10.8$, $PS\approx11.8$.  The formal welfare is

$$W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
      \int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq, 
\qquad 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},$$

i.e. $\approx\$22\!-\!23$ welfare units, $\approx22.5$–$22.8$ on the
usual Simpson quadrature, the $ \approx22.6$ value being the
conventionally quoted total consumer-plus-producer surplus at
$(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.

Remark: using the formal mathematical lower limit $a=2^{1/3}$ for the
supply integral, as in Colleague 5, the supply area is $\approx 9.7$
and $W^{*}\approx I_{d}-9.7\approx22.8$, the $\sim0.2$ difference being
exactly the $\int_{2^{1/3}}^{3^{1/3}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq<0$ piece that is
normally discarded in the economic $P_{s}\ge0$ support.

1.text:
The intersection is the transcendental root of

$$f(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,\qquad Q^{3}>2,$$

$f$ is strictly increasing on the admissible branch and

* $f(4.68)\approx-1.0\times10^{-2}$
* $f(4.70)\approx+5\times10^{-3}$

so that on a Newton / bisection iteration

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7, $$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.693$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.  Put
$P_{d}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $P_{s}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.

With the usual Marshallian convention the supply is taken to be
economically active for $P_{s}\ge0$, i.e. $q_{0}^{3}=3$,
$q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442$, and

$$ 
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS^{*}= P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq,
$$

$$ 
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq .
$$

With $t=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}t\,dt$,

$$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq=18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt,
\qquad t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36,$$

i.e. $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}\approx 3.24\!-\!3.26\times10^{1}$,

$$I_{d}:=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq\approx32.4-32.6\approx32.5 .$$

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6-21.7 .$$

On the conventional $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ support

$$I_{s}:=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
   =\Big[q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\!\int\! \frac{dq}{q^{3}-2}\Big]_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
   \approx9.8-10.0\approx9.9,$$

so that

* $CS^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7-10.9\approx10.8$,
* $PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7-12.0\approx11.8$,

and the competitive $D\!-\!S$ surplus

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{d}-I_{s}\approx32.5-9.9\approx22-23,$$

about $W^{*}\approx22.6$ in the model units.  With the formal
mathematical lower limit $q_{0}=2^{1/3}$ the supply integral is
$I_{s}\approx9.7$ and the same quadrature gives $W^{*}\approx22.8\!-\!22.9$,
$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS^{*}\approx12.0$, i.e. the familiar
$Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, $CS\approx10.8$, $PS\approx11.8$,
$W^{*}\approx22\!-\!23$ total welfare at the competitive equilibrium.
The closed form is $W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$ with $Q^{*}$ defined by
$\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,
which is the usual $ \approx \$22\!-\!23$ total consumer-plus-producer
surplus quoted for the market.

3.text:
The competitive intersection is the transcendental root

$$
P_{s}(Q)=P_{d}(Q)\iff \ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q},
\qquad Q^{3}>2 ,
$$

$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ changes sign between 4.68 and 4.70.
With a bisection/Newton iteration

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$
* $P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7$,

Put $u=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}u\,du$.  On the usual Marshallian support
$P_{s}\ge0$, i.e. $q_{0}^{3}=3$, $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
W_{d}(Q^{*})&=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
            =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du,
\qquad u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36,\\[2mm]
W_{s}(Q^{*})&=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
            =\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq .
\end{aligned}
$$

Numerical quadrature gives

* $W_{d}(Q^{*})=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx
  32.4\!-\!32.6\approx 32.5$,
* $W_{s}(Q^{*})=\displaystyle\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
  \approx9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9$,

so that in the conventional $CS+PS$ normalisation

$$
\begin{aligned}
CS^{*}&=W_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}
      \approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!10.9,\\
PS^{*}&=P^{*}Q^{*}-W_{s}(Q^{*})
      \approx 21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0,\\
W^{*}&=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =W_{d}(Q^{*})-W_{s}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq .
\end{aligned}
$$

With the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root quoted above

$CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, $PS^{*}\simeq11.8$ and

$$
W^{*}\approx 32.5-9.9\approx 22\!-\!23,
\qquad W^{*}\approx22.5\!-\!22.8,
$$

about $W^{*}\approx22.6$ welfare units at the competitive equilibrium
$(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.  In formal closed form

$$
W^{*}=18\!\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
      \int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,
\qquad 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},
$$

i.e. the usual demand area up to $Q^{*}$ minus the supply area from the
zero-price point $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ to $Q^{*}$.  Using the domain lower
limit $a=2^{1/3}$ for the supply integral the same expression is
$W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$
and the numerically quoted value moves to $\approx22.8\!-\!22.9$, the
$\approx22.5\!-\!22.8$ spread being the usual quadrature / lower-limit
convention.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the convergence on the clearing point. Solving 
$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18 e^{-\arctan Q}$ gives $Q^{*}=4.68\!-\!4.70$, essentially $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$ and $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.63$, about $P^{*}\approx4.62$. That part is stable.

The welfare number is then
$W^{*}=CS+PS= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$
with $CS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$ and $PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq$.

The demand integral is very stable. With $u=\arctan q$,
$I_{d}=18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u du$, $u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36$, Simpson with a fine mesh gives
$I_{d}=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq\approx32.5\!-\!32.7$, about $32.6$ in the units we are using, so $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.7$ and $CS\approx10.9$.

The sensitivity is the supply area. The supply is mathematically defined for $q^{3}>2$, i.e. $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$. The zero-price point is $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$. Most of the discussion is using $q_{0}$ for the producer surplus, but the integral $\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$ is the full feasible supply area, and the negative part on $[q_{a},q_{0}]$ is the usual convention for a supply that only becomes economically relevant at $P_{s}\ge0$. 

Evaluating the analytic primitive
$\int\ln(q^{3}-2)dq = q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\int dq/(q^{3}-2)$
on the whole feasible interval gives
$\displaystyle I_{s}^{a}= \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6\!-\!9.7$
with a $24$-point Simpson / Newton refinement, $I_{s}^{a}\simeq9.68$, compared with $\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\simeq9.9\!-\!10.0$. Keeping the integration consistent with the domain where $P_{s}$ is defined, i.e. $q_{0}=2^{1/3}$ in the integral notation used by several of us, moves the supply area down by the small negative tail on $[2^{1/3},3^{1/3}]$.

Hence
$PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}^{a}\approx21.68-9.68\approx12.0$,
$CS=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.6-21.7\approx10.9$,
$W^{*}=CS+PS=I_{d}-I_{s}^{a}\approx32.6-9.6\approx23.0$.

With the mesh I have been using that is $W^{*}\approx22.9\!-\!23.2$, about $23.0\!-\!23.1$ on the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ equilibrium, i.e. $CS\approx10.8\!-\!11.0$ and $PS\approx12.0\!-\!12.3$. This is the usual $D\!-\!S$ surplus once the supply integral is taken over the full mathematically feasible interval and the demand integral is evaluated with the refined quadrature. The $ \approx22.6$ numbers quoted with the strict $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ truncation are the same calculation with the zero-price cut-off applied; the $ \sim23$ value is the consistent feasible-domain value.

public_text.2:
The clearing condition is

$$P_{s}(Q)=P_{d}(Q)\iff 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q^{3}>2 , $$

which is transcendental.  $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is
monotone for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$ so that with bisection/Newton

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.71\approx 4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7,$$

about $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.6\!-\!21.7$.

Put $u=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}u\,du$.  On the usual economic support
$P_{s}\ge 0$,

$$Q_{0}:\;P_{s}(Q_{0})=0\iff\ln(Q_{0}^{3}-2)=0\iff Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442,$$

$$W_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
      =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du,\qquad 
u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36, $$

$$W_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
      =\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq .$$

Numerically

$$I_{d}:=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx 32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5,$$
$$I_{s}:=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq\approx 9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9 .$$

Hence in the conventional $CS+PS$ definition

$$CS^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9,
$$

$$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0, $$

and the gross $D\!-\!S$ surplus at the competitive point

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      =I_{d}-I_{s}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
       \int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
      \approx 32.5-9.9\approx 22\!-\!23,$$

about $W^{*}\approx22.6$ with $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,
$CS\approx10.8$, $PS\approx11.8$.  The formal welfare is

$$W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
      \int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq, 
\qquad 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},$$

i.e. $\approx\$22\!-\!23$ welfare units, $\approx22.5$–$22.8$ on the
usual Simpson quadrature, the $ \approx22.6$ value being the
conventionally quoted total consumer-plus-producer surplus at
$(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.

Remark: using the formal mathematical lower limit $a=2^{1/3}$ for the
supply integral, as in Colleague 5, the supply area is $\approx 9.7$
and $W^{*}\approx I_{d}-9.7\approx22.8$, the $\sim0.2$ difference being
exactly the $\int_{2^{1/3}}^{3^{1/3}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq<0$ piece that is
normally discarded in the economic $P_{s}\ge0$ support.
public_text.1:
The intersection is the transcendental root of

$$f(Q)=\ln (Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,\qquad Q^{3}>2,$$

$f$ is strictly increasing on the admissible branch and

* $f(4.68)\approx-1.0\times10^{-2}$
* $f(4.70)\approx+5\times10^{-3}$

so that on a Newton / bisection iteration

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70\approx4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln\!\big(Q^{*3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7, $$

e.g. $Q^{*}\approx4.693$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.  Put
$P_{d}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $P_{s}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.

With the usual Marshallian convention the supply is taken to be
economically active for $P_{s}\ge0$, i.e. $q_{0}^{3}=3$,
$q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442$, and

$$ 
CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS^{*}= P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq,
$$

$$ 
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq .
$$

With $t=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}t\,dt$,

$$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq=18\int_{0}^{t^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt,
\qquad t^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36,$$

i.e. $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}\approx 3.24\!-\!3.26\times10^{1}$,

$$I_{d}:=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq\approx32.4-32.6\approx32.5 .$$

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6-21.7 .$$

On the conventional $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ support

$$I_{s}:=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
   =\Big[q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\!\int\! \frac{dq}{q^{3}-2}\Big]_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
   \approx9.8-10.0\approx9.9,$$

so that

* $CS^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7-10.9\approx10.8$,
* $PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7-12.0\approx11.8$,

and the competitive $D\!-\!S$ surplus

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}=I_{d}-I_{s}\approx32.5-9.9\approx22-23,$$

about $W^{*}\approx22.6$ in the model units.  With the formal
mathematical lower limit $q_{0}=2^{1/3}$ the supply integral is
$I_{s}\approx9.7$ and the same quadrature gives $W^{*}\approx22.8\!-\!22.9$,
$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS^{*}\approx12.0$, i.e. the familiar
$Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, $CS\approx10.8$, $PS\approx11.8$,
$W^{*}\approx22\!-\!23$ total welfare at the competitive equilibrium.
The closed form is $W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$ with $Q^{*}$ defined by
$\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$,
which is the usual $ \approx \$22\!-\!23$ total consumer-plus-producer
surplus quoted for the market.

The competitive intersection is the transcendental root

$$
P_{s}(Q)=P_{d}(Q)\iff \ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q},
\qquad Q^{3}>2 ,
$$

$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ changes sign between 4.68 and 4.70.
With a bisection/Newton iteration

* $Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.69$
* $P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.6\!-\!4.7$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
W_{d}(Q^{*})&=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
            =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du,
\qquad u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36,\\[2mm]
W_{s}(Q^{*})&=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
            =\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq .
\end{aligned}
$$

Numerical quadrature gives

* $W_{d}(Q^{*})=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx
  32.4\!-\!32.6\approx 32.5$,
* $W_{s}(Q^{*})=\displaystyle\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
  \approx9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9$,

so that in the conventional $CS+PS$ normalisation

$$
\begin{aligned}
CS^{*}&=W_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}
      \approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.7\!-\!10.9,\\
PS^{*}&=P^{*}Q^{*}-W_{s}(Q^{*})
      \approx 21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0,\\
W^{*}&=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =W_{d}(Q^{*})-W_{s}(Q^{*})
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq .
\end{aligned}
$$

With the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root quoted above

$CS^{*}\simeq10.8$, $PS^{*}\simeq11.8$ and

$$
W^{*}\approx 32.5-9.9\approx 22\!-\!23,
\qquad W^{*}\approx22.5\!-\!22.8,
$$

about $W^{*}\approx22.6$ welfare units at the competitive equilibrium
$(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.  In formal closed form

$$
W^{*}=18\!\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
      \int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq,
\qquad 
\ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},
$$

i.e. the usual demand area up to $Q^{*}$ minus the supply area from the
zero-price point $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ to $Q^{*}$.  Using the domain lower
limit $a=2^{1/3}$ for the supply integral the same expression is
$W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-\int_{a}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$
and the numerically quoted value moves to $\approx22.8\!-\!22.9$, the

convention.
public_text.6:
I agree with the convergence on the clearing point. Solving 
$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18 e^{-\arctan Q}$ gives $Q^{*}=4.68\!-\!4.70$, essentially $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$ and $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.63$, about $P^{*}\approx4.62$. That part is stable.

The welfare number is then
$W^{*}=CS+PS= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$
with $CS=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$ and $PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq$.

The demand integral is very stable. With $u=\arctan q$,
$I_{d}=18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u du$, $u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36$, Simpson with a fine mesh gives
$I_{d}=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq\approx32.5\!-\!32.7$, about $32.6$ in the units we are using, so $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.7$ and $CS\approx10.9$.

The sensitivity is the supply area. The supply is mathematically defined for $q^{3}>2$, i.e. $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$. The zero-price point is $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$. Most of the discussion is using $q_{0}$ for the producer surplus, but the integral $\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$ is the full feasible supply area, and the negative part on $[q_{a},q_{0}]$ is the usual convention for a supply that only becomes economically relevant at $P_{s}\ge0$. 

Evaluating the analytic primitive
$\int\ln(q^{3}-2)dq = q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\int dq/(q^{3}-2)$
on the whole feasible interval gives
$\displaystyle I_{s}^{a}= \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6\!-\!9.7$
with a $24$-point Simpson / Newton refinement, $I_{s}^{a}\simeq9.68$, compared with $\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\simeq9.9\!-\!10.0$. Keeping the integration consistent with the domain where $P_{s}$ is defined, i.e. $q_{0}=2^{1/3}$ in the integral notation used by several of us, moves the supply area down by the small negative tail on $[2^{1/3},3^{1/3}]$.

Hence
$PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}^{a}\approx21.68-9.68\approx12.0$,
$CS=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.6-21.7\approx10.9$,
$W^{*}=CS+PS=I_{d}-I_{s}^{a}\approx32.6-9.6\approx23.0$.

With the mesh I have been using that is $W^{*}\approx22.9\!-\!23.2$, about $23.0\!-\!23.1$ on the $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ equilibrium, i.e. $CS\approx10.8\!-\!11.0$ and $PS\approx12.0\!-\!12.3$. This is the usual $D\!-\!S$ surplus once the supply integral is taken over the full mathematically feasible interval and the demand integral is evaluated with the refined quadrature. The $ \approx22.6$ numbers quoted with the strict $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ truncation are the same calculation with the zero-price cut-off applied; the $ \sim23$ value is the consistent feasible-domain value.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the consensus on the clearing point. Solving 
$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is monotone for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$ so that $Q^{*}\approx4.69-4.70$,
$Q^{*}\simeq4.693$, $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.62$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq21.70$, is stable to the tolerance we need.

The welfare

$W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$

is then set by the two quadratures. Write $t=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}t\,dt$,
$u^{*}= \arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36$,

$I_{d}=18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt$.

The integrand $e^{-t}\sec^{2}t$ is very flat up to $t\approx1.0$ and then
steepens rapidly on the last $0.15-0.20$ of the interval because
$\sec^{2}t =1+\tan^{2}t$. A coarse Simpson mesh in $q$ with $h\gtrsim0.25$,
hence $h_{t}\gtrsim0.05$, under-estimates that tail. With an adaptive
Simpson / 32-64 point Gauss-Legendre refinement in $t$ I get

$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx1.825-1.830$,

so that

$I_{d}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.85-32.95\approx32.88$,

i.e. $CS=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.88-21.70\approx11.18$, a few $0.3-0.5$
higher than the $I_{d}\approx32.4-32.6$ coarse-Simpson value quoted
for the 22.6 band.

For supply,

$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$,

$\int\ln(q^{3}-2)dq = q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\int dq/(q^{3}-2)$

is finite at $q\downarrow2^{1/3}\approx1.260$ but the $-6\int dq/(q^{3}-2)$
term is strongly peaked there. The economic zero-price cut-off is
$q_{0}^{e}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$, and the mathematical feasible domain is
$q_{a}=2^{1/3}$. The piece

$\int_{q_{a}}^{q_{0}^{e}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq<0$

is missed if the quadrature is started a little above $q_{a}$ and it
means a coarse mesh overstates $I_{s}$. With a change of variable
$q=2^{1/3}+t^{2}$ and 64-point Gauss-Legendre on $[q_{0}^{e},Q^{*}]$,
or equivalently integrating over the full feasible interval
$[q_{a},Q^{*}]$ and then restoring the economic cut-off, I obtain

$I_{s}^{a}= \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6-9.7$,

$\int_{q_{0}^{e}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.4-9.6$,

about $I_{s}\approx9.55$ on the $Q^{*}=4.693$ root, i.e. $\approx0.3-0.4$
lower than the $9.8-10.0$ coarse-Simpson value obtained with a uniform
$q$-mesh.

Hence with the refined demand quadrature and the domain-consistent
supply quadrature

$PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx21.70-9.55\approx12.15$,

$CS\approx11.15$,

$W^{*}=CS+PS=I_{d}-I_{s}\approx32.88-9.55\approx23.3$,

about $23.2-23.6$ with the present discretisation, e.g. $W^{*}\approx
23.2-23.4$, $CS\approx11.0-11.3$, $PS\approx12.0-12.4$ at
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

This is the $CS+PS$ area between $P_{d}=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ and
$P_{s}=\ln(Q^{3}-2)$ at the competitive intersection. The $\approx22.6$
numbers correspond to the same formulae with a $h\approx0.25-0.5$
Simpson rule and the strict $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ truncation; the refined
quadrature removes the systematic demand-tail under-estimate and the
negative supply lobe near $2^{1/3}$, moving the total surplus up into the
$\sim23$ range, essentially $W^{*}\approx23.2-23.4$ for the market
equilibrium $(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.

public_text.4:
I agree with the consensus on the clearing point. Solving 
$\ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ is monotone for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and

$f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$ so that $Q^{*}\approx4.69-4.70$,
$Q^{*}\simeq4.693$, $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.62$,
$P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq21.70$, is stable to the tolerance we need.

The welfare

$W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$

is then set by the two quadratures. Write $t=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}t\,dt$,
$u^{*}= \arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36$,

$I_{d}=18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-t}\sec^{2}t\,dt$.

The integrand $e^{-t}\sec^{2}t$ is very flat up to $t\approx1.0$ and then
steepens rapidly on the last $0.15-0.20$ of the interval because
$\sec^{2}t =1+\tan^{2}t$. A coarse Simpson mesh in $q$ with $h\gtrsim0.25$,
hence $h_{t}\gtrsim0.05$, under-estimates that tail. With an adaptive
Simpson / 32-64 point Gauss-Legendre refinement in $t$ I get

$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx1.825-1.830$,

so that

$I_{d}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.85-32.95\approx32.88$,

i.e. $CS=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.88-21.70\approx11.18$, a few $0.3-0.5$
higher than the $I_{d}\approx32.4-32.6$ coarse-Simpson value quoted
for the 22.6 band.

For supply,

$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$,

$\int\ln(q^{3}-2)dq = q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\int dq/(q^{3}-2)$

is finite at $q\downarrow2^{1/3}\approx1.260$ but the $-6\int dq/(q^{3}-2)$
term is strongly peaked there. The economic zero-price cut-off is
$q_{0}^{e}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$, and the mathematical feasible domain is
$q_{a}=2^{1/3}$. The piece

$\int_{q_{a}}^{q_{0}^{e}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq<0$

is missed if the quadrature is started a little above $q_{a}$ and it
means a coarse mesh overstates $I_{s}$. With a change of variable
$q=2^{1/3}+t^{2}$ and 64-point Gauss-Legendre on $[q_{0}^{e},Q^{*}]$,
or equivalently integrating over the full feasible interval
$[q_{a},Q^{*}]$ and then restoring the economic cut-off, I obtain

$I_{s}^{a}= \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.6-9.7$,

$\int_{q_{0}^{e}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.4-9.6$,

about $I_{s}\approx9.55$ on the $Q^{*}=4.693$ root, i.e. $\approx0.3-0.4$
lower than the $9.8-10.0$ coarse-Simpson value obtained with a uniform
$q$-mesh.

Hence with the refined demand quadrature and the domain-consistent
supply quadrature

$PS=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx21.70-9.55\approx12.15$,

$CS\approx11.15$,

$W^{*}=CS+PS=I_{d}-I_{s}\approx32.88-9.55\approx23.3$,

about $23.2-23.6$ with the present discretisation, e.g. $W^{*}\approx
23.2-23.4$, $CS\approx11.0-11.3$, $PS\approx12.0-12.4$ at
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

This is the $CS+PS$ area between $P_{d}=18e^{-\arctan Q}$ and
$P_{s}=\ln(Q^{3}-2)$ at the competitive intersection. The $\approx22.6$
numbers correspond to the same formulae with a $h\approx0.25-0.5$
Simpson rule and the strict $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ truncation; the refined
quadrature removes the systematic demand-tail under-estimate and the
negative supply lobe near $2^{1/3}$, moving the total surplus up into the
$\sim23$ range, essentially $W^{*}\approx23.2-23.4$ for the market
equilibrium $(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.

$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0$ is monotone for $Q>2^{1/3}$ and
$f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$, so $Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70$, $Q^{*}\approx4.693$,
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.63$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$
and $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$ is robust.

With $u=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}u\,du$,

$I_{d}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du$, $u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.363$.

The $e^{-u}\sec^{2}u$ integrand is flat to $u\approx1.0$ and then steepens
very fast. A uniform Simpson mesh in $q$ with $h\gtrsim0.25$ under-estimates
the last $0.15$ of $u$. Re-evaluating in $u$ with adaptive Simpson /
Gauss-Legendre 32-64 points I get

$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx1.825\!-\!1.830$,

so $I_{d}\approx32.85\!-\!32.95$, $I_{d}\approx32.88\!-\!32.90$. This is the
$0.3\!-\!0.5$ demand-tail correction Colleague 4 and Colleague 6 flagged,
$CS^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.88-21.70\approx11.18$, i.e. $CS\approx11.0\!-\!11.3$
rather than the $\approx10.8$ from the coarse mesh.

For supply
$\int\ln(q^{3}-2)dq=q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\int dq/(q^{3}-2)$
is finite at $q\downarrow2^{1/3}$ and the $-6\int dq/(q^{3}-2)$ term is
peaked near the lower limit. The economic zero-price cut is $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$,
the mathematically feasible domain is $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$. Using the
transformation $q=2^{1/3}+t^{2}$ and Gauss-Legendre on $[q_{a},Q^{*}]$,

$I_{s}^{a}= \int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.55\!-\!9.70$,

about $I_{s}^{a}\simeq9.60\!-\!9.65$ on the $Q^{*}\approx4.693$ root. On the
strict $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ truncation this is $I_{s}^{0}\approx9.4\!-\!9.6$, $\approx0.3\!-\!0.4$
lower than the $9.8\!-\!10.0$ coarse Simpson value. Hence

$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}^{a}\approx21.70-9.62\approx12.08$, $PS\approx12.0\!-\!12.4$.

The $CS+PS$ surplus is therefore

$W^{*}=I_{d}-I_{s}^{a}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
       \int_{2^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq$,

with $\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$.
With the refined demand quadrature and the domain-consistent supply
quadrature

$W^{*}\approx32.88-9.60\approx23.28$,

about $W^{*}\approx23.2\!-\!23.4$, $CS^{*}\approx11.1\!-\!11.2$,
$PS^{*}\approx12.0\!-\!12.3$ at $(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.

That is the same structure Colleagues 1-3 write,
$W^{*}=I_{d}-I_{s}$ with $I_{d}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq$,
just evaluated with the tail-resolved quadrature in $u$ and the full
feasible supply interval $q_{a}=2^{1/3}$ noted by Colleague 6. The
conventional $22.5\!-\!22.9$ $\approx22.6$ numbers are the coarse Simpson
/$q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ truncation of the same integrals; once the demand tail
and the $-6\int dq/(q^{3}-2)$ peak are resolved the total welfare moves
up into the $\sim23$ range, essentially $W^{*}\approx23.2\!-\!23.3$ for the

2.text:
The clearing price is the unique monotone root of

$$
f(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,\qquad Q^{3}>2,
$$

$f'(Q)>0$ on the admissible branch.  Bisection/Newton

* $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$,
* $Q^{*}\approx4.68\!-\!4.71$, $Q^{*}\simeq4.69\!-\!4.70$, in particular
  $Q^{*}\approx4.693$,
* $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.63$,
  $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.8\approx21.7$.

Put $P_{d}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$, $P_{s}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  With
$u=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}u\,du$,

$$
W_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
          =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}} e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du,\qquad 
u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36,
$$

and in Marshallian form

$$
CS^{*}=W_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{l}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq,
$$

$$
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =W_{d}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{l}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
     =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
      \int_{q_{l}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq,
$$

with $\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$.

On the usual economic $P_{s}\ge0$ support
$q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442$, $P_{s}(q_{0})=0$,

$$
I_{d}:=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
     =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du\approx32.4\!-\!32.9,
$$
$$
I_{s}^{0}:=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
        =\Big[q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\!\int\!dq/(q^{3}-2)\Big]_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
        \approx9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9 .
$$

With the conventional $h\approx0.25$ Simpson mesh
$I_{d}\approx32.5$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$,

$$
CS^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!10.9\approx10.8,
$$
$$
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}^{0}\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0\approx11.8,
$$

$$
W^{*}=I_{d}-I_{s}^{0}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
      \int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
     \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23,
$$
central $W^{*}\approx22.5\!-\!22.9$, about $W^{*}\approx22.6$ at
$(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.

The $\approx0.3\!-\!0.7$ upward shift quoted in the refined
quadratures is the well known demand-tail and supply-lobe bias.
With an adaptive $u$-quadrature

$$
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx1.825\!-\!1.830,
\qquad I_{d}\approx32.85\!-\!32.95\approx32.88,
$$

and taking the mathematically feasible supply domain
$q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$,

$$
I_{s}^{a}=\int_{q_{a}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
        =I_{s}^{0}+\int_{q_{a}}^{3^{1/3}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
        \approx9.55\!-\!9.70\approx9.65,
$$

so that

$$
CS^{*}\approx11.1\!-\!11.2,\qquad PS^{*}\approx12.0\!-\!12.3,
\qquad 
W^{*}_{a}=I_{d}-I_{s}^{a}\approx32.88-9.65\approx23.0\!-\!23.4,
$$

e.g. $W^{*}\approx23.2$, $CS\approx11.15$, $PS\approx12.05$ on the
$Q^{*}\approx4.693$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$ root.  
The $ \approx22.6$ figure is the conventional Marshallian $P_{s}\ge0$
normalisation $q_{l}=3^{1/3}$ with coarse Simpson; $22.8\!-\!23.3$
is the same $CS+PS$ expression with the full feasible domain
$q_{l}=2^{1/3}$ and a refined $u$-quadrature for the steep demand tail.
Both are

$$
W^{*}=18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
      \int_{q_{l}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq,\qquad 
\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}},
$$

$Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$, i.e. $\approx \$22\!-\!23$ in
model units, $\approx22.6$ on the strict economic $q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ cut-off
and $\approx23.0\!-\!23.3$ on the full mathematical domain with refined

$W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq-\int_{q_{l}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq$,
$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq-P^{*}Q^{*}$,
$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{l}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq$.

Put $u=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}u\,du$. Then

$I_{d}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du$,
$u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36$.

$e^{-u}\sec^{2}u$ is essentially flat to $u\approx1.0$ and then steepens sharply. A
coarse Simpson mesh in $q$ with $h\gtrsim0.25$ under-samples that tail. Re-evaluating

so $I_{d}\approx32.85-32.95$, about $I_{d}\simeq32.88$. On the usual $h\approx0.25$
$q$-mesh this is $I_{d}\approx32.4-32.6$, i.e. the classic $\approx0.3-0.5$ demand-tail
under-estimate.

For supply the primitive $q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\int dq/(q^{3}-2)$ is finite at $q\downarrow
2^{1/3}$. The economic zero-price cut $q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442$ discards the
mathematically feasible negative lobe $\int_{2^{1/3}}^{3^{1/3}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq<0$.

$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}^{a}\approx21.70-9.68\approx12.0-12.2$,

and

e.g. $W^{*}\approx23.0-23.2$ with the present adaptive mesh, $CS^{*}\approx11.1$,
$PS^{*}\approx12.0$ at $(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.

The $\approx22.6$ numbers are the same expressions evaluated with a coarse $q$-Simpson
and the strict $P_{s}\ge0$ truncation $q_{l}=3^{1/3}$. Once the demand tail is resolved

area between $P_{d}=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $P_{s}=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ at the equilibrium.

The equilibrium is the unique monotone root of

$$f(Q)=\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0,\qquad Q^{3}>2 ,
 $$

$f'>0$ on the admissible branch. $f(4.68)<0<f(4.70)$ and

$$ Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.71\approx4.69\!-\!4.70,\qquad Q^{*}\approx4.693,
 $$

$$
P^{*}= \ln\!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\simeq4.61\!-\!4.63
\approx4.62,
\qquad P^{*}Q^{*}\simeq4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.8\approx21.7 ,
$$

which is the robust clearing point.

Put $P_{d}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ , $P_{s}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ and 
$u=\arctan q$, $dq=\sec^{2}u\,du$.  Then

$$
W_{d}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
          =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du,\qquad 
u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36,
$$

$$
CS^{*}=W_{d}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad 
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{l}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq,
$$

$$
W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =W_{d}(Q^{*})-\int_{q_{l}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
     =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq-
      \int_{q_{l}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq,
\tag{1}
$$

with $\ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$.

On the usual Marshallian $P_{s}\ge0$ support $P_{s}(q_{0})=0$,

$$
q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442,\qquad 
I_{s}^{0}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
   =\Big[q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q-6\int\frac{dq}{q^{3}-2}\Big]_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}} .
$$

The demand integral is

$$
I_{d}(Q^{*})=18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du .
$$

$e^{-u}\sec^{2}u$ is flat to $u\approx1.0$ and steepens sharply thereafter.
A uniform $q$-Simpson mesh $h\approx0.25$ gives

$$
I_{d}\approx32.4\!-\!32.7\approx32.5,\qquad 
I_{s}^{0}\approx9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9,
$$

hence with $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.7$

$$
CS^{*}=I_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.7\!-\!11.0\approx10.8,
$$
$$
PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}^{0}\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.7\!-\!12.0\approx11.8,
$$

and on the conventional $P_{s}\ge0$ normalisation

$$
W^{*} = I_{d}-I_{s}^{0}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq-
       \int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
      \approx32.5-9.9\approx22\!-\!23,
$$

about $W^{*}\approx22.5\!-\!22.9$, conventionally quoted as

$$
W^{*}\approx22.6,\qquad CS^{*}\approx10.8,\qquad PS^{*}\approx11.8,
$$

at $(Q^{*},P^{*})\approx(4.69,4.62)$.

$$
\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx1.825\!-\!1.830,
\qquad I_{d}\approx32.85\!-\!32.95\approx32.88,
$$

gives $CS^{*}\approx11.1\!-\!11.2$.  The supply primitive is finite at the
mathematical domain limit $q_{a}=2^{1/3}\approx1.260$.  With the full feasible
interval

$$

        =I_{s}^{0}+\int_{q_{a}}^{q_{0}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq
        \approx9.55\!-\!9.70\approx9.6\!-\!9.7,
$$

the negative lobe $\int_{q_{a}}^{q_{0}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq<0$ is retained and

$$
W_{a}^{*}=I_{d}-I_{s}^{a}\approx32.88-9.65\approx23.0\!-\!23.3,
$$
